--- Respondents The Court made the following Judgment:
Challenge in this Motor Accidents Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is to the Award, dated 05.10.2015, in M.V.O.P. No.202 of 2012 on the file of Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-District Judge, Chittoor (for short, 'the Tribunal') whereunder the Tribunal, AVRB,J dealing with a claim of compensation made by the claimants for Rs.9,00,000/-, on account of the death of M.K. Naveen Kumar (hereinafter referred to as 'the deceased'), in a motor vehicle accident, which was occurred on Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport ... vs Smt. M.K. Janaki on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137573858/
1 20.04.2011 at about 03:45 PM, awarded a sum of Rs.5,36,000/- towards compensation, with interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit against the respondent.

The Tribunal apportioned the compensation as a sum of Rs.1,60,800/- each to the first and second petitioners and Rs.1,07,200/-
each to the third and fourth petitioners respectively.
2. The parties to this Appeal will hereinafter be referred to as described before the Tribunal, for the sake of convenience.

3. The case of the claimants, in brief, according to the averments set out in the claim, before the Tribunal, is that first and second petitioners are the parents and third and fourth petitioners are the brother and sister of the deceased.

The deceased died on the spot on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident occurred on 20.04.2011 on Chittoor - Tirupati road in front of Vinayaka Temple near Chittoor Co-operative Sugar Factory.

The APSRTC bus bearing No.AP 10 Z 8554, being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, came from Chittoor side and dashed motorcycle bearing No.AP 03 AA 9875, being driven by one G.U. Kumar with the deceased as pillion rider and thereby both of them fell down and sustained injuries and G.U. Kumar died on the way to hospital and the deceased died on the spot.

The Station House Officer, Chittoor Traffic Police Station registered a case in Crime AVRB,J No.42 of 2011 for the offence under Section 304-A IPC and after due investigation filed charge sheet in C.C. No.399 of 2011 on the file of the Court of Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Chittoor against the driver of the offending vehicle.

entities.text: Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Chittoor
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The respondent being owner of the bus is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
As on the date of accident, the deceased was a student of B.Com., III Year in VCR Degree College, Chittoor.
Claimants lost the deceased on account of the sudden accident.
The deceased was earning Rs.4,500/- p.m. by employing himself as a paperboy.
Hence, the claim.

4. Respondent got filed a counter denying the averments in the petition and contending in substance that the claimants have to prove the manner of the accident, age, occupation and income of the deceased.
Claim is excessive.
Accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the bike on which the deceased was travelling as a pillion rider.
Hence, the claim is to be dismissed.

5. The Tribunal, on the basis of the aforesaid pleadings, settled the following issues for trial:
1. Whether the accident in question occurred was due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of APSRTC bus bearing No.AP 10 Z 8554 or the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.AP 03 AA 9875?
AVRB,J 2.
Whether the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for any compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?

sentences.text: To what relief?
6. During the course of trial on behalf of the claimants before the Tribunal, PWs.1 and PW.2 were examined and Exs.A-1 to A-6 were marked.
On behalf of the respondent, no evidence was adduced and no documents were marked.

7. The Tribunal, on hearing both sides and after considering the oral and documentary evidence on record, answered the issues in favour of the petitioners and against the respondent and awarded a sum of Rs.5,36,000/- towards compensation, as above.
8. The un-successful respondent/APSRTC, feeling aggrieved of the aforesaid award, filed the present Appeal.

9. Now in deciding the present Appeal, the simple question that falls for consideration is:
Whether the Award of the Tribunal in M.V.O.P. No.202 of 2012, dated 05.10.2015, on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-District Judge,
Chittoor, is sustainable under law and facts and whether there are any grounds to interfere with the same?

Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-District Judge,
Chittoor
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
AVRB,J POINT:
10.
Sri K. Viswanatham, learned Standing Counsel for the appellants/APSRTC, would submit that appropriate orders may be passed on merits.
11. No arguments are advanced on behalf of the respondents/petitioners.

12. According to the contention of the appellant, in the grounds of Appeal, the Tribunal erred in holding that the accident was occurred on account of the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending bus and also erred in awarding the compensation.
13. Turning to the evidence of PW.1, who is the mother of deceased, she deposed in tune with her pleadings and through her examination, Exs.A-1 to A-6 were marked.
14. Petitioners got examined PW.2, witness to the occurrence, who deposed that on 20.04.2011, he along with one Pichandi were going on the two wheeler.
He found that the deceased along with one G.U. Kumar were coming in their opposite direction on a motorcycle bearing No.AP03 AA 9875 towards Chittoor side.
The offending vehicle overtook their vehicle and hit the motorbike driven by G.U.Kumar.
Both the rider and pillion rider fell down.
15. As evident from the evidences of PW.1 and PW.2 before the Tribunal, nothing could be elicited to disbelieve their testimony.
There is no dispute that the FIR was laid against the driver of the AVRB,J offending vehicle under Ex.A-1.
The cause of death was on account of the fatal injuries received in the accident.

The accident occurred was not due to any mechanical defect as per Ex.A-2 - Accidental Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport ... vs Smt. M.K. Janaki on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137573858/
3 Inspector Report.

entities.text: Accidental Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport ... vs Smt. M.K. Janaki
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Police, after conclusion of investigation, filed charge sheet under Ex.A-6 alleging that the driver of the offending vehicle drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and caused the death of the deceased.
There was no rebuttal evidence on the part of the respondent.
Hence, the Tribunal rightly held that the accident occurred was due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
16. Turning to the quantum of compensation, there is no dispute that the petitioners are no other than father, mother, brother and sister of the deceased.
They are dependents on the deceased.
The evidence of PW.1 and the other evidence prove the fact that the deceased was employed himself as a paperboy.

The Tribunal did not believe the theory of the petitioners that he was getting an income of Rs.4,500/- p.m., but considering that he employed himself as a paperboy, ascertained the income of the deceased as Rs.3,000/- p.m. on notional basis and awarded a sum of Rs.1,500/- p.m. towards future prospects.

Thereby the Tribunal arrived at the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.4,500/-
p.m.

The Tribunal deducted half of the amount towards his personal and living expenses and computed the loss of earnings as Rs.2,250/- x 12 x 18, thereby the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.4,86,000/- and Rs.50,000/- towards funeral expenses, loss of estate and loss of love and affection.
It is to be noted that the Tribunal relied upon a AVRB,J decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Santosh Devi v. National Insurance Company Limited and others1 to award the future prospects.

entities.text: Santosh Devi v. National Insurance Company Limited and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is to be noted that the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others2 is very clear regarding the future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: According to the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi (2nd supra), if the deceased was self employed and below the age of 50 years, addition of 40% of the established income should be warranted.
So, the act of the Tribunal in awarding 50% towards future prospects needs to be interfered with and the income is to be arrived at by adding 40% of the annual income towards the future prospects.
So, if the notional income of Rs.3,000/- and 40% thereof is to be computed, it would come to Rs.4,200/- p.m.

As the deceased was a bachelor, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and others3, half of the amount is to be deducted as such the contribution of the deceased towards his family members would be around Rs.2,100/- p.m.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and others3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no dispute that according to the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma (3rd supra), appropriate multiplier relevant to the age group of the deceased is 18 as such the multiplicand to be arrived at is Rs.2,100/- x 12 x 18 , which would come to Rs.4,53,600/-.
The amount of compensation to be awarded under the heads of funeral expenses and loss of estate in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Pranay Sethi (2nd supra) is Rs.30,000/-.
As the 2012 ACJ 1428 2017 ACJ 2700 2009 ACJ 1298 AVRB,J deceased was aged about 23 years, first and second petitioners being parents of the deceased are not entitled to receive filial consortium.

Hence, the claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.4,53,600/- +
Rs.30,000/-, which would come to Rs.4,83,600/-.
Considering the same, Award of the Tribunal needs to be interfered with to such an extent.

17. In the result, the Motor Accidents Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is allowed in part reducing the compensation awarded by the Tribunal from Rs.5,36,000/- to that of Rs.4,83,600/- with interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The appellant/APSRTC is directed to deposit rest of the compensation amount, if any, within a period of one month from this date.

On such deposit, the compensation awarded by this Court i.e., Rs.4,83,600/- is to be Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport ... vs Smt. M.K. Janaki on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137573858/
4 apportioned as that of Rs.1,60,800/- each to the first and second petitioners i.e., parents and Rs.81,000/- each to the third and fourth petitioners being brother and sister of the deceased.

sentences.text: No order as to costs.
Consequently, Miscellaneous Applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
